newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler sees world car market share of 2.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Daimler sees world car market share of 2.2 pct.

text.p: New car models should help Daimler-Benz AG capture 2.2 percent of the world car market within a couple of years, up from its current 1.6 percent share, Chairman Juergen Schrempp said on Wednesday.

Speaking at the company's annual shareholder meeting, Schrempp said that despite the company's widening offering of new cars that range from the small A-Class to the super-luxury S-Class, Daimler was not becoming a "mass producer" of cars.
He said the company would continue to build on its exclusive image and produce only top quality cars.
Daimler, which expects to sell 700,000 cars this year, is planning to sell 200,000 A-Class models a year by 1999 once full production begins. In 1998, Daimler expects to make 180,000 A-Class cars.

In addition to the A-Class, for which Daimler said it has 350,000 customer enquiries in Germany, Daimler will also soon start selling a sport utility vehicle, the M-Class which is being made in the U.S.
A Daimler spokesman said incoming orders for the car have been higher than expected.
